newsitem.title: NORWAY: Waigel says Germany will do all to meet Maastricht.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Germany will do all to meet Maastricht.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday his country would do everything it can to fulfill Maastricht criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"We will do everything to meet these criteria, including the deficit goal," Waigel told reporters before a conference with Nordic and Baltic finance ministers.
He said the latest German unemployment figures -- 4.66 million in January -- fitted into the country's plans to meet the criteria.
The single currency, or euro, is scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999. But 1997 economic data will be used to decide which EU members take part at the start.
The Maastricht Treaty sets a budget deficit ceiling of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year for candidate countries to qualify for the launch of the single currency.
The German government has projected a budget deficit target of 2.9 percent of GDP, but analysts question whether it can achieve it.
